<div class="content">
  <p> I am interested in economics, geopolitics, and applied statistics, particularly in the gap between elegant theory and messy reality. Models matter, but so do incentives, institutions, uncertainty, and the limits of the data in front of you.

My academic background is in economics and business analytics. I want to work in economics, and in time I hope to pursue deeper study in statistics as well.

This blog is where I work through ideas in public. Sometimes that means writing about policy or markets. Sometimes it means testing an argument, following a question further than expected, or trying to understand why a neat model breaks down in practice.

I also host the Forecasting Impact Podcast, focused on forecasting across industry and academia.</p>
